title: TextBFGS: A Case-Based Reasoning Approach to Code Optimization via Error-Operator Retrieval

mechanism.domainTask: Case-based LLM optimization of executable code using error-operator retrieval
mechanism.populationDetail: The search iteratively updates one current code variable; a separate case base stores error/operator trajectories rather than candidate code individuals.
mechanism.archiveDetail: The Hessian-Proxy Case Base stores error descriptions and abstract correction operators, not elite solution code.
mechanism.replacementDetail: The current code variable advances through sequential updates while successful error/operator cases are appended to separate trajectory memory; the paper does not specify incumbent acceptance/tracking fully.
mechanism.generationDetail: One current code variable is revised using the current error diagnosis and retrieved abstract operators; the full code artifact is editable and no localized edit boundary is specified.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Execution results condition the current update; successful `(gradient, operator)` pairs are appended to memory and later retrieved by gradient similarity.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: The current code is the only true parent. Top-k retrieved cases are memory references keyed by gradient/error similarity, not parent solutions.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: A semantic quasi-Newton/case-based update retrieves abstract correction operators by error-gradient similarity and retains successful error-to-operator trajectories.

provenance.citationWarning: Do not classify the case base as a candidate or elite archive: it stores error/operator cases, not solutions. Replacement of the current code and best-state handling are underspecified, while successful cases are append-only. The retrieved top-k cases are references, not true parents.
